observations.task_scope: Create an auditable automated unit, integration, E2E, and failure-injection matrix covering quota, 429, auth, network, 5xx, and malformed SSE behavior.
observations.starting_point: The package has 186 Node test rows and separate Linux/systemd workflows, but no single manifest proves suite classification, required fault coverage, or matrix completeness.
observations.implemented_matrix: Every checked-in Node test file belongs to exactly one unit, integration, or E2E suite; unclassified, duplicate, failed, inconsistent, timed-out, or skipped rows fail the release gate.
observations.required_faults: Dedicated loopback proxy tests cover quota, generic 429 with bounded Retry-After, auth, network disconnect, upstream 5xx, and truncated malformed SSE, plus explicit before/after semantic SSE boundaries.
observations.runtime_compatibility_fix: The first Node 22 CI run exposed that unref on the status-bridge deadline timer could let the process exit while a timeout-protected request remained pending; keeping the timer referenced restores the bounded deadline contract.
observations.strict_linux_result: GitHub Actions run 30250040183 passed 196/196 with zero skips on both Node 22.23.1 and Node 24.18.0, including three fixture UI smoke scenarios per runtime.
observations.protocol_boundary: M6.1 may automate fixture and pinned-checkout E2E paths, but it does not waive the user-deferred M0.3, M3.5, or M4.1 real-account evidence gates.

residual_risks: Automated E2E uses pinned upstream source and fixture services/UI states; it does not invoke a real account or prove account-bound response-chain portability.
The strict matrix ran on Ubuntu x64; the complete M6.1 suite did not run on arm64.
Real-account switching remains outside M6.1 by user direction; no seamless continuity claim is supported.
The mandatory M6.2 24-hour soak test remains pending.
